response:
## Verdict

The findings are strong and the P0 work is exactly right. The *plan* re-commits the error the findings diagnose: you concluded that 100% of effort went to the measuring apparatus, then ordered the work apparatus-first, with the only lever-1 item at P3 gated behind a decision you've already answered. Fix the sequencing and the priority taxonomy and this is a good plan.

## The four things I'd change

**1. P3 isn't gated on P1 — unblock it now.** P3 says building-skills iter4 and the optimizing-context re-measure both wait "AFTER P1 settles the re-measure bar." But your own evidence paragraph already argues for option (b), and (b) doesn't block iteration: you reshape now and enroll in the next G≥8 batch. As written, the one lever that produces adopter-felt value is behind a formality. Promote it, and if the owner's /decide queue is the constraint, iter4 should be starting in parallel with the decision, not after it.

**2. Option (b) needs an edit taxonomy, or the 18-commit problem recurs verbatim.** "Honest scope + re-measure debt ledger" is a labeling change, not a process change. What prevents commit 19 is a stated rule for which edits incur re-measure debt and which don't. You already have three items implicitly claiming the exemption — #302's four reference edits (explicitly below MDE), P0 item 8's constant de-hardcoding, and the P0 cite fixes themselves. Name the class: cite/path repairs, char-negative reshapes, and edits whose plausible effect is below the current MDE do not incur debt and may not claim improvement; anything else enters the ledger. Without that, (b) means "we stopped promising," and the ledger grows unbounded.

Related: P1 conflates two debts. Re-measure debt (edited after measuring) and never-measured-at-all (sweep, per your own /sweep section). The honest-scope language has to cover both, or the README still overclaims.

**3. The C5 pre-reg is the most important item in the document and it's sub-bullet (iii) of a killed grid.** "building-skills vs bare — Anthropic itself claims the skill shouldn't need to exist; live loss condition for ours" is the existential test for your flagship artifact. Make it a top-level track. And notice the ordering conflict with P3: you're planning iteration 4 of building-skills while proposing an experiment that could show it shouldn't exist. Run the bare baseline first, or state explicitly that you're investing in iter4 ahead of that answer and why.

**4. The ADOPT track is the largest number in the document and has no section.** ~10pd for the Inspect AI swap appears only in the status header — no tier, no kill criterion, no relation to anything else. Two things it needs: (a) whether swapping substrate invalidates comparability with prior benchmark dirs — if it does, the swap and the batched G≥8 re-measure must be co-scheduled or you pay twice; (b) an honest note that a substrate swap *is* apparatus work and competes directly with lever 1 under your own stop-list. Say which wins if you can't do both.

## Section notes

**#317 is the weakest recommendation.** You conclude n-grams understate the real coupling (the DV is house doctrine — "frontmatter order," "cut Background"), then adopt an n-gram overlap report as the standing caveat. A report reading 1.4–3.6% will be read as "contamination is small" when your own analysis says the real contamination is semantic and invisible to the metric. Either label it explicitly as a verbatim-only floor, not a bound, or skip it. Bigger gap: you require task-value outcomes for *future* benchmarks but say nothing about the *existing* building-skills and engineering-principles verdicts scored on the contaminated DV. That's a live truth-in-labeling item and belongs in the README caveat by name, not folded into "instrument unconverged."

**#310 round 2 is already re-inflating.** It now carries fix-verification, the control-integrity class, ADR 0098's backlog, *and* "smaller adoptions ride round 2." That's how one consolidated round becomes rounds 2–6 again. Cap it: written exit criterion and a hard artifact count before it starts, and move the adoptions elsewhere.

**Power arithmetic is applied asymmetrically.** You killed the $25 grid on MDE grounds — correct — but never state cost-per-G-unit × required G × number of skills for the batched re-measure you endorse. If that bill is unaffordable, (b) isn't honest scope, it's a permanent IOU, and the README should say "unmeasured since 19-Jul" rather than promise batches. Do the multiplication and put it in the doc.

**Rename sequencing is backwards.** ADR 0097 "executes LAST" but the rename touches every path, cite, and tombstone that P0 items 4/5/7 just repaired. Either move it ahead of the cite work or budget the redo explicitly. Also worth one line in the retired-ids map: benchmark dirs published under the old name create a permanent split identity in the artifact record.

**P0 item 8 isn't actionable as written.** A SKILL.md can't "defer to the script" at read time. Pick a mechanism: a generated block, or a test that fails when the text drifts from validate.py, or drop the numbers and cite the script.

**Frame P0 item 9 as one defect, not three lows.** 6.6x→"7x", the "3+ cases" floor in four files, and the ADR 0016 omission are the same failure: claims drift toward the author's favor and nothing checks them. ADR 0096 is the systemic fix — say so, and consider a check that fails on unsourced numeric claims. Otherwise you'll re-file these next quarter.

## Two structural additions

**Split the document.** Right now the header tracks status, the verdict states findings, and P0–P3 mix shipped with open. A reader can't tell what's left without cross-referencing nine numbered items against the header. Three sections: open decisions (with recommended answer, owner, date), open work (sequence + cost), shipped (collapsed).

**Give the headline finding teeth.** "Self-referential spiral" has no tripwire. Add one: e.g., if the next 14 days of merges are again >50% apparatus, instrument work stops until a lever-1 artifact ships. And pre-write the recommended answer for every /decide so the owner approves rather than derives — grok's "route them in one sitting" advice applies to this document as a whole, not just #310. One person's decision queue is currently the critical path for P1, four P2s, P2b, P3's gate, and the ADOPT track, which is a sufficient explanation for why lever 1 gets nothing.
